story.h2: You published it. Google may not have noticed.
story.body: New and updated pages can sit for a long time without being crawled or indexed, and nothing tells you which ones.

story.h2: See what can stop a page from being indexed
story.body: Paste any page address to see whether Google can index it. The checker tests the HTTP status and redirects, robots.txt rules for Googlebot, the X-Robots-Tag header, meta robots noindex, the canonical tag and how much content is in the HTML. Each problem comes with a plain-English fix. No sign-up needed.
story.note: The checker shows whether a page can be indexed. It does not show whether it is in Google right now; connect your site to see that.

story.body: Crawl, submit through Google's official Indexing API, and verify with Google's URL Inspection.

steps.title: Connect your site
steps.body: Create a Google service account and add it as an Owner in Search Console. Our step-by-step guide takes about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Crawl and submit
steps.body: Crawl your site, import a sitemap, or paste URLs. Scheduled crawls find new and changed pages and submit them through Google's Indexing API for you.

steps.title: Watch it index
steps.body: Each URL moves from queued to submitted to indexed. Every submitted URL is re-checked with Google's URL Inspection 1, 3 and 7 days later.

story.body: In your dashboard, status is Google's own URL Inspection result for every URL, re-checked 1, 3 and 7 days after submission, not an estimate.

chart.title: Coverage over time
chart.illustrationLabel: Illustration, not customer data. Timing depends on your site and on Google.
chart.note: Pages Google is told about tend to be picked up sooner than pages it has to discover from a sitemap, but there is no guaranteed timing.

story.h2: Official API. Your own Google quota.
story.body: We use Google's publicly documented Indexing API with your own Google Cloud project, so its 200 submissions a day are yours, and we never work around that quota. "Indexed" means Google says so.

points.title: Automatic retries with backoff
points.body: Page fetches retry three times with exponential backoff, and every background job gets three attempts before it is marked failed with a reason you can read.

points.title: Locked, non-overlapping runs
points.body: A site that is already crawling cannot be queued twice. Each run holds a lock until it completes, so parallel schedules never collide or double-submit.

points.title: Quota-aware queue
points.body: Google allows 200 Indexing API requests per project per day. We track usage against Google's Pacific-time reset, warn you before you hit it, and hold the rest for the next window.

points.title: Live progress streams
points.body: Crawls, bulk submissions and status syncs stream progress to your dashboard as they happen, with automatic reconnect if the connection drops.

points.title: Verified against Google
points.body: Status sync pulls coverage and indexing state per URL from Google's URL Inspection, not from a guess.

points.title: Real-browser, robots-aware crawling
points.body: Pages render in a headless Chromium so JavaScript-driven sites are read correctly. Sitemaps are parsed and robots.txt rules are respected on every crawl.

checker.intro: Paste any page address to see whether Google can index it. Each problem comes with a plain-English fix. No sign-up needed.

tests.name: Status and redirects
tests.body: Does the page answer 200 OK? Redirect chains, temporary redirects, 404s, 403s and server errors all stop or delay indexing.

tests.name: robots.txt
tests.body: Evaluated the way Googlebot does it. We show the exact line that blocks the page.

tests.name: Noindex
tests.body: Both places Google reads it: the meta robots or googlebot tag in the HTML and the X-Robots-Tag HTTP header.

tests.name: Canonical
tests.body: If the canonical tag points somewhere else, Google usually indexes that URL instead of this one.

tests.name: Content
tests.body: Pages with very little text, or whose text only appears after JavaScript runs, are often left out of the index.

tests.name: HTTPS
tests.body: Google prefers the HTTPS version of a page; plain HTTP pages are flagged.

faq.a: We crawl your site, send new and changed pages to Google through its official Indexing API, and then check each URL with Google's URL Inspection so you can see what was actually indexed and, if not, why.

faq.q: Is this allowed for my pages?
faq.a: Google officially supports the Indexing API for pages with JobPosting or BroadcastEvent structured data. For other pages a submission asks Google to crawl sooner but cannot guarantee indexing, and Google screens all submissions for spam. You use your own Google project, so its 200 submissions a day are yours, and we never work around that quota. The crawl, the URL Inspection status and the explanations of why a page is not indexed work for every page regardless.

faq.q: Does it work for existing pages?
faq.a: Yes. You can submit both new pages and updated existing pages, so Google sees your latest content.
Any website with publicly accessible URLs: WordPress, WooCommerce, Shopify, nopCommerce, Next.js, or fully custom-built sites.

faq.q: The checker says Google can index my page. Why isn't it in Google?
faq.a: Being indexable means nothing stops Google; it doesn't mean Google chose to index it. Search Console reports such pages as 'Discovered, currently not indexed' or 'Crawled, currently not indexed'. Usually the fix is more unique content, internal links to the page, and asking Google to crawl it, which GoogleIndexing.com does for you through the Indexing API.

faq.q: Does the checker tell me whether my page is in Google right now?
faq.a: No. Only Search Console knows for sure; a site: search is often wrong. Connect your site to GoogleIndexing.com (free plan available) and every URL is checked with Google's URL Inspection, including the date Google last crawled it.
